name: 26681-longprefill-llama70bfp8-8gpu
hardware: 8x H100 80GB HBM3, all eight GPUs of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=8, PP=1, DP=1 -- one vLLM engine on one node; both degrees are pinned.
architecture: dense decoder (LlamaForCausalLM, 80 layers, 64 query heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden 8192, intermediate 28672, window 131072); NVIDIA ModelOpt per-tensor FP8 linear weights with static scales, lm_head excluded, norms/residuals/KV bf16, ~72.7 GB of safetensors.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=1, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 200 requests with a 3600 s safety cap, static seed 26681. The cap is a guard rail, not an operating point: the 200-request bound is what ends a healthy run, and the cap is sized so that a 72.7 GB weight load plus whole-graph compilation cannot eat into the request budget.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, single turn: every request is exactly 8192 prompt tokens and 2 output tokens. Prefix caching is off. The chat template adds 35 tokens, so the engine sees 8227 per request.
purpose: A document analysis service running a 70-billion-parameter model on eight GPUs, handling one long eight-thousand-token request at a time.
launch:
# An operating point, declared once and used unchanged.

model: nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8
tensor-parallel-size: 8
pipeline-parallel-size: 1
enable-prefix-caching: false

# HAZARD: the engine's reader takes `key: value` lines only and skips indented ones, so
# `compilation-config` MUST stay on one line or the key never reaches the engine.
compilation-config: {"level": 3, "pass_config": {"enable_sequence_parallelism": true, "enable_async_tp": true}, "use_inductor_graph_partition": false, "splitting_ops": [], "custom_ops": ["+quant_fp8"], "cudagraph_mode": "FULL"}

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.6
max-num-batched-tokens: 8448
max-model-len: 16384

# Pinned deliberately. Without it the KV cache is whatever the memory profiler leaves over.
num-gpu-blocks-override: 8192

dtype: bfloat16
